text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- U.S. sources in Washington said the United States would expand its role in Middle East from mediation to arbitration and suggesting solutions.

- Prime Minister Kamal Ganzouri ends his tour of Asia today and will give President Hosni Mubarak a report on it when he returns. In Shanghai he said that Egypt had started to lay the legislative structure to attract international investment.

- Mubarak will make an important speech at celebrations of Labour Day organised by the Trade Union Federation for April 30. He will talk about Egypt's success at economic reform, the role of workers in the next phase and the commitment to protect the rights of workers in the privatisation programme.
- Foreign Minister Amr Moussa received a message from Palestinian President Yasser Arafat yesterday. It contained a Palestinian assessment of the peace process.
- The Cabinet will discuss on Thursday the draft of a standardised companies law, to take the place of all the existing laws on setting up companies.

- Agriculture Minister Youssef Wali said the final stages of the law on relations between landlords and tenants of agricultural land will be implemented with the consent of both parties, especially as the area rented for agriculture will increase under the new law.
- Ganzouri said the government was studying the question of direct flights between Egypt and Southeast Asia.
- Amr Moussa told reporters that the peace process must be saved and could not be left to its fate. It must be brought out of the bottleneck, he added.
- Schools and universities resume work today after the Eid.
- Ugandan President Yoweri Museveni will visit Egypt for a few days soon, Amr Moussa said.
